learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to shift focus in a sentence! Master the rules to convert Active Voice (focus on the doer) to Passive Voice (focus on the action/receiver) across all tenses.

main_concepts.simple_explanation:
1. Bring the Object to the front (make it the new subject). 
2. Apply the correct 'Be' helping verb according to the tense. 
3. ALWAYS use V3 (Past Participle of the main verb). 
4. Add 'by' + the original Subject (new object). 
Active: 'Ram (S) killed (V2) Ravan (O).' ➔ Passive: 'Ravan (O) was killed (V3) by Ram (S).'

• Present Simple (V1): is/am/are + V3. 
• Past Simple (V2): was/were + V3. 
• Continuous (is/am/are + ing): is/am/are + BEING + V3. 
• Perfect (has/have/had + V3): has/have/had + BEEN + V3.

For any Modal (can, could, should, must, will, shall), simply add 'BE' + V3. 
Active: 'I can lift this box.' ➔ Passive: 'This box can BE lifted by me.'

Sentences starting with a verb (Order/Command). Rule: 'Let' + Object + 'be' + V3. 
Active: 'Open the door.' ➔ Passive: 'Let the door be opened.' 
For Requests: Use 'You are requested to...' (e.g., 'Please sit down' ➔ 'You are requested to sit down').

fun_activity.title: 🎯 Who takes the Spotlight?
fun_activity.instructions: Active voice is a superhero movie where the hero (Subject) is in focus: 'Batman caught the thief.' Passive voice is a news report where the event (Object) is in focus: 'The thief was caught (by Batman).' News reporters LOVE passive voice because the action is more important than who did it!

exam_tips: 📌 Pronoun changes: I ➔ me, We ➔ us, He ➔ him, She ➔ her, They ➔ them. (And vice-versa).
📌 ALWAYS remember: Passive voice CANNOT be made without the 3rd form of the verb (V3). If your passive answer doesn't have V3, it is 100% wrong!
📌 4 Tenses CANNOT be changed into Passive Voice: Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect Continuous, Future Perfect Continuous, and Future Continuous.
quick_recap: ⭐ Intransitive verbs (verbs without an object like sleep, go, laugh, die) cannot be changed into Passive Voice.
⭐ When a sentence has two objects (Direct and Indirect), you can make two different passive sentences. (e.g., 'He gave me a pen' ➔ 'A pen was given to me by him' OR 'I was given a pen by him').
⭐ Interrogative sentences remain interrogative in passive voice (e.g., 'Do you play cricket?' ➔ 'Is cricket played by you?').
